newsitem.title: DUBAI: Small BCCI depositors in UAE to be repaid in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Small BCCI depositors in UAE to be repaid in Dec.

text.p: Small depositors in United Arab Emirates (UAE) branches of the failed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) will be reimbursed in full in December, the UAE liquidation administrators said on Tuesday.
They said in a statement that UAE depositors with deposits of up to 20,000 dirhams ($5,450) on July 5, 1991, would be reimbursed fully by the UAE Central Bank in December.
BCCI, founded in Luxembourg in 1972, was shut down in 1991 with debts of more than $12 billion after evidence emerged of widespread money laundering.
In the UAE there are about 45,000 creditors, owed nearly five billion dirhams.

"As regards claims of the rest of depositors and non-depositors admitted by the Luxembourg Court, the global liquidators will dispatch the approved amounts for the benefit of these claimants in December 1996 through the UAE liquidators," the statement said.

Liquidators of the failed bank said in May that an agreement with majority shareholder, the Abu Dhabi government, was a major step towards paying the first dividend to about 250,000 creditors worldwide.
Under the agreement Abu Dhabi, the biggest of the seven emirates forming the UAE, paid $1.8 billion into a pool for distribution to creditors and depositors.
